drive: From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906, then continue onto Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) and follow it 1.1 miles to the Alpental lots; park in the upper lot.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District) — Boulder River Wilderness
storedPass: Assume Northwest Forest Pass required at the trailhead (standard for MBS NF day-use trailheads) — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From Darrington via Squire Creek Road to the gated washout parking, then the Squire Creek Walls climbers' path

Drive Highway 16 (the Yellowhead) to Mount Robson Provincial Park, about 90 km west of Jasper and a short way east of the Highway 5 junction near Valemount. Turn off at the Mount Robson visitor centre and follow the paved side road about 2 km to the trailhead parking lot at its end. Check the park's trail status before you go: the trail closed after flood damage in 2021 and reopened in full in 2025.

names: Adirondak Loj / High Peaks Information Center
SR 20 pullout near milepost 166 (Burgundy Col trail)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District, Okanogan County, Washington. The surrounding designation is given as the North Cascades Scenic Highway corridor.
storedPass: None. A Northwest Forest Pass is specifically NOT required, because parking is on the state highway shoulder rather than at a Forest Service trailhead.
None. A Northwest Forest Pass is specifically NOT required, because you park on the state highway shoulder rather than at a Forest Service trailhead.
drive: From the roadside pullout near milepost 166 on SR-20, ~3 miles east of the Washington Pass hairpin; short approach to the wall

landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Darrington Ranger District (Henry M. Jackson Wilderness)

drive: From the Bedal Creek Trailhead at the end of FR-4096 off the Mountain Loop Highway (~2,790 ft), via Bedal Creek Trail #705

names: Sol Duc Trailhead (end of Sol Duc Hot Springs Road)

names: Staircase Trailhead (North Fork Skokomish, Olympic NP)

NPS park pass
drive: From Hoodsport on US-101, drive about 16 miles on the paved and gravel road to the Staircase developed area.

names: NF-77 roadside pullout (Mosquito Meadows area, Randle)

storedPass: N/A

names: Deception Crags and Mt Washington trailhead
drive: Take I-90 Exit 38, turn right at the bottom of the ramp onto SE Homestead Valley Road, and take the next right onto the gravel road up a small hill to the trailhead. A Discover Pass is required.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Chelan Ranger District) — Glacier Peak Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at some trailheads (fee day-use sites) — $5/day or $30/year.
None for the Holden boat-and-shuttle approach; a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is only required to park at the Phelps Creek/Trinity trailhead used by the Spider Gap alternative.
drive: From Holden Village (~3,300 ft) — reached by Lake Chelan ferry to Lucerne and the village shuttle — via the Railroad Creek Trail

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at some trailheads (fee day-use sites) — $5/day or $30/year.
None — there is no road to Stehekin; the High Bridge trailhead is reached by the NPS valley shuttle.
drive: Via the Lady of the Lake ferry to Stehekin and the NPS shuttle to High Bridge, then the Agnes Creek / PCT trails

landManager: Glacier Peak Wilderness, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Wenatchee River Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required for trailhead parking ($5 day-use ePass or $30 annual)
Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From the White River Trailhead (~2,300 ft) at the end of White River Road / FR-6400 above Lake Wenatchee

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Skykomish Ranger District
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency Recreation Pass accepted (WA Discover Pass is NOT valid here)
Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
drive: From US 2 at Baring, near milepost 41, turn north onto 635th Place NE, cross the railroad tracks, keep left at the junction, and continue onto Forest Road 6024 for about 4 miles to the Barclay Lake trailhead.

landManager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (Mt. Adams Ranger District) — Mount Adams Wilderness
storedPass: No trailhead parking pass is required at the Killen Creek Trailhead. The Mount Adams Climbing Pass applies separately above 7,000 ft.
No trailhead parking pass is required. A free, self-issued wilderness permit is required to enter the Mt. Adams Wilderness and is available at the trailhead.
drive: From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground, pass the campground and continue just under 4.5 miles to the trailhead.

names: North Fork Quinault Trailhead (North Shore Road)
North Fork Quinault Trailhead (North Shore Road, road's end)
landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
Wilderness Annual Pass optional; separate park entrance fee/pass applies for vehicle entry.
drive: From US-101 at milepost 126, turn onto South Shore Road and follow it 12.9 miles to the Quinault River bridge; cross it, turn right onto North Shore Road, and drive 3.5 miles to the road end at the trailhead and ranger station.

names: Depot Creek Road washout (via Chilliwack Lake, BC)
landManager: North Cascades National Park (entirely on the US side, along the Custer-Rahm ridge)
storedPass: No parking permit required at the Depot Creek trailhead.

No day-use pass, but a wilderness camping permit is required for any overnight trip. Effectively also requires a passport or enhanced driver's license, since the drive-in and most of the lower approach trail pass through British Columbia before re-entering the US at the Monument 65 border marker.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: Start at the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead (large lot at the end of FR 56).

names: SR-20 pullout below Summertime Crag (east of Washington Pass)

storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).

Leave Highway 2 on Whitepine Road and go about 1 mile to parking just before the road runs under the railroad trestle.

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)

drive: From Marblemount, leave SR-20 onto Cascade River Road (FR-15) and drive to milepost 22.5, where a small pullout is on the left opposite Johannesburg Mountain. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is rough gravel; the road can close at the Eldorado parking area at milepost 20.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Stuart Lake, Eightmile, and Snow Lakes trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (overnight permit holders get a covering parking pass instead).
Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful Pass
drive: Start at the Snow Lakes Trailhead (paved, day-use permit required, ~4 miles up Icicle Creek Road from Leavenworth).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Entiat Ranger District
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful Pass
Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency (America the Beautiful) Pass, or the trailhead's $5/day Digital Day Pass — required specifically at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead
drive: From Entiat, drive Entiat River Road up the valley about 32 miles, turning right onto FR-5606 two miles past Silver Falls campground; follow FR-5606 steeply uphill about 4 miles to the trailhead.

names: PCT North Trailhead (Snoqualmie Pass, I-90 Exit 52)
landManager: Alpine Lakes Wilderness — Cle Elum Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (jointly managed with Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF)

Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful/Interagency Pass
drive: From I-90 take Exit 52 (West Summit), turn left under the freeway onto Alpental Road, take the first right after 0.1 mile, and where the road splits after another 0.1 mile, bear right for the main lot.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (Pasayten Wilderness)

Northwest Forest Pass, Digital Day Pass or Interagency pass at Canyon Creek Trailhead; none at the East Bank Trailhead.
